Async worker guide

This guide explains how to run a small asynchronous worker and keep each result attached to its source. The examples show real indentation and a table of options so readers can compare behaviour without guessing.

Run a worker

Use asyncio.run(main()) to enter the loop. Read the task cancellation reference and the external guide before changing the timeout. Keep the original indentation when copying this example.

async def main():
    for item in ["甲", "乙"]:
        print(item)

asyncio.run(main())

Options

These options control the operation. A body budget counts returned characters, while a timeout counts elapsed waiting time. Use both controls when reading several remote pages together.

OptionMeaning
timeoutMaximum waiting time
limitMaximum body length
